artifacts.summary: Re-derives both measured lint-coverage gaps (books files absent from Check C/G arrays with formatting defects beyond omission; 11-of-23 evidenced research-agent subset for the new bounded-wait check), rules on the line-wrap brittleness (hold unwrapped by convention) and the curated-array mechanism (keep, add a completeness-net check), and sweeps both existing arrays for further absentees (none found beyond the two books files, one edge case flagged).

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lint/lint-agent-contracts.sh, a curated in-scope array (Check C/G/H pattern) being absent from an array produces 0 lint failures, not a visible red -- the per-file check loop only ever visits array members. Before trusting 'lint passes' as evidence of coverage, diff the full dispatchable-agent enumeration (frontmatter-gated: first line '---', a 'name:' key) against each curated array to find silent omissions.

When classifying whether a research/implementation agent is genuinely exposed to a Bash-backgrounding risk, a generic tool-grant phrase like 'Run verification commands, build scripts, tests' is not itself evidence of exposure -- grep the whole file for an actually-realized, concretely-named command (lake build, pytest, cargo, pnpm, a specific .sh script). Several agent-system/extensions/formal/* agents share identical unrealized boilerplate text with zero concrete build/test invocation anywhere in the file.
